Notice Regarding California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determinations
Pursuant to CEQA, a "project" is defined as a "whole action" subject to a public agency's discretionary funding or approval that has the potential to either (1) cause a direct physical change in the environment or (2) cause a reasonably foreseeable indirect physical change in the environment. "Projects" include discretionary activity by a public agency, a private activity that receives any public funding, or activities that involve the public agency's issuance of a discretionary approval and is not statutorily or categorically exempt from CEQA. (Pub. Res. Code § 21065.) To the extent that matters listed in this Agenda are considered “projects” under CEQA, their appropriate CEQA determination will be listed below each recommendation. If no CEQA determination is listed, it has been determined that the action does not constitute a “project” under CEQA.
Viewing City Council Meetings
Members of the public may view the City Council meeting live on the City’s website https://www.azusaca.gov/1389/Watch-Meetings-Online, or on Channel 3 (Spectrum). Archived video of recorded meetings is also available on the City website. Your attendance at this public meeting may result in the recording and broadcast of your image and/or voice as previously described.
Procedures for Addressing the Council
The Council encourages interested people to address this legislative body by making public comments. Public comments may be made during designated agendized public comment periods and during public hearing items. Public comments are limited to five (5) minutes per speaker, unless a different time is announced by the Mayor/presiding Chair.
The Council encourages free expression of all points of view. To allow all persons the opportunity to speak, please keep your remarks brief. If others have already expressed your position, you may simply indicate that you agree with a previous speaker. If appropriate, a spokesperson may present the views of your entire group. State law generally prohibits the City Council from responding to or acting upon matters not listed on this agenda. Council rules prohibit clapping, booing, or shouts of approval or disagreement from the audience. Clapping, booing, shouting or other actions from the audience which, disturbs, impedes, or otherwise renders infeasible the meeting’s orderly conduct, who, after a request by the presiding officer, refuses to cease such behavior may be removed from the City Council chambers or remote participation platform.

  MONDAY, OCTOBER 20, 2025

The City Council of the City of Azusa met in Closed and Regular session at Azusa Auditorium at 213 E.
Foothill Blvd., Azusa, CA 91702.

Mayor Gonzales called the meeting to order at 6:30 P.M.

ROLL CALL: Roll call was taken by City Clerk Cornejo.

PRESENT:  COUNCILMEMBERS: GONZALES, ALVAREZ, AVILA, MENDEZ, BOW

Lieutenant Chivas, City Clerk Services Manager Juarez, Director of Economic and Community Development
Jimenez, Director of Public Works Delgadillo, Director of Community Resources Carpenter, City Librarian
Hassen, General Manager of Utilities Singh, Environmental Programs Specialist Sagun, I.T. Manager Arreola

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Arturo Rincon.

The Invocation was led by Deacon Mike Flores, Saint Frances of Rome Church.

CLOSED SESSION

Interim City Attorney Casso announced that there was no reportable action for Closed Session Items 1–3 and
Item No. 5, and that he had recused himself from Item No. 4.

City Manager Gonzalez reported on Item No. 4, stating that the Council received a report from Staff and
provided direction. There was no reportable action.

CEREMONIAL

1. Presentation of a Proclamation proclaiming the month of October as Domestic Violence Awareness Month
  in the City of Azusa

Councilmember Bow presented a proclamation in honor of Domestic Violence Awareness Month.

California Senator Susan Rubio thanked the City Council for bringing attention to this important issue;
highlighted key state bills related to domestic violence for the community’s awareness; stated that she is present
to represent individuals who have lost their lives due to domestic-violence-related incidents; and encouraged the
community to speak with their children about domestic violence to recognize early signs and stay safe;
presented the YWCA with a certificate, joined by the Azusa City Council, in recognition of their efforts to raise
awareness for domestic violence.

City Council Minutes  Page | 2
October 20, 2025
 Alexis Sanchez, District Representative from Assemblywoman Blanca Rubio, thanked the YWCA and the City
of Azusa for recognizing October 2025 as Domestic Violence Awareness Month.

PUBLIC PARTICIPATION

The following individuals expressed concerns regarding Item D-2 on the agenda; mentioned the importance of
sales from the firework booths to nonprofit organizations; recommended reviewing SB 1403; and urged the
Council to leave the vote up to the community: Cecilia Ford, Anthony Alvarez, Isabel Tapia, John Kelley, and
Victoria Perez.

Farheen Rizvi, resident and founder of a nonprofit organization called Human Mind Exploration & Expansion
(Human MEE), stated that the organization designs projects and experiments for participants to become more
compassionate and engaging human being; expressed interest in partnering with the Azusa Police Department to
organize a session for the community; and asked for guidance and assistance in getting in contact with the
appropriate individual to make that happen.

City Clerk Cornejo announced that the following individuals submitted written public comment and copies were
forwarded to the City Council: Salomon Jimenez, Raymond Noriega, Desiree Jimenez, Celeste Rangel, Isai
Rangel, Adrienne Alvarez, Melanie Ortega, Johnny Sanchez, Jimmy Sanford, Steven Abasta, Dan Simpson,
Carmen Sanchez, Gomez Family, Sandra Gallegos, William Eagleson, Flora Wilcox, Joe Casas, bgcasas.

REPORTS, UPDATES, AND ANNOUNCEMENTS FROM STAFF/COUNCIL

“Pet of the Month” Presentation

Los Angeles County Animal Control Officer Arrighi-Bracci introduced “Romeo,” a one-and-a-half-year-old
Terrier currently available for adoption.

City Manager Communications

City Manager Gonzalez thanked the residents, the Golden Days Committee, City departments, and local
organizations for a wonderful celebration of the 77th Annual Golden Days event.

Councilmember Announcements

Mayor Pro Tem Alvarez announced the “Let’s Get Spooky: Flicks on Route 66” movie night in the Historic
Auditorium on October 25; thanked the City Clerk/Golden Days Chairman for the successful Golden Days
event; and suggested adding more vendors at the Golden Days Carnival.

Councilmember Avila announced the Azusa Canine & Companion Costume Contest at Memorial Park on
October 23; reported his attendance at the League of California Cities Conference in Long Beach; thanked the
Golden Days Committee and Staff for their hard work on the Golden Days festivities; offered his thoughts and
prayers to the Azusa student who was struck by a vehicle on his way to school; encouraged residents to drive
slowly and safely in the mornings for the protection of children; and requested that the meeting be adjourned in
honor of Lori Ulloa.

Councilmember Mendez congratulated the Golden Days Committee on a successful event; reported that the 3rd
Annual Día de los Muertos event will take place on November 1, 2025, at the NRC; and extended his thoughts
and prayers to the Azusa High School student who was struck by a vehicle earlier that morning.

Councilmember Bow offered acknowledgment to Azusa Golden Days Chairman Cornejo for an excellent week
of events; thanked City staff who were the backbone of the logistics and safety of the festivities; and thanked
the Azusa Police Department for their fast action at Saturday’s event and for keeping residents safe; announced
that on November 6, 2025, at Memorial Park, the City will be hosting a “Fall into Wellness Fair”; and shared
information on Domestic Violence Awareness for the month of October.

Mayor Gonzales reported that he attended the League of Cities Conference in Long Beach; thanked the Golden
Days Committee for a great week of events; and mentioned the continued violence at the Golden Days Carnival,
requesting that City staff take federal action on the individuals involved.

City Clerk Cornejo thanked all who participated in the successful 77th annual Golden Day’s Event.

INTRODUCTION AND CONSIDERATION OF ORDINANCE NO. 2025-06, RESCINDING AND
REPLACING ARTICLE IV (FIREWORKS) OF CHAPETR 30 (FIRE PREVENTION AND PROTECTION)
OF THE CITY OF AZUSA MUNICIPAL CODE IN ITS ENTIRETY AND ADOPTING A NEW ARTICLE
IV (FIREWORKS), AND ADOPTING A NOTICE OF EXEMPTION REGARDING SAME, AND MAKING
FINDINGS IN SUPPORT THEREOF

Deputy City Manager De Anda-Scaia presented proposed Ordinance No. 2025-07 amending City’s Municipal
Code to prohibit the sale and discharge of fireworks within the City, effective July 5, 2027; stated that at the
August 18, 2025 City Council meeting, an in-depth discussion was held regarding the long-term liability and
safety concerns of the existing fireworks policy; noted that the Council received testimony from City Staff, the
Police Department, and various non-profit organizations that rely on fireworks sales as a fundraising source.

He reported that the Council had reached a majority consensus to bring back an amended municipal policy for
consideration at a future meeting; provided a recap of the existing policy, which allows the use of “safe and
sane” fireworks within designated areas of the City and permits non-profit organizations to apply annually for
fireworks booth sales; and added that Azusa remains the only City along the foothills that still allows such sales.

Mr. De Anda - Scaia further stated that the proposed amendment would rescind the applicable section of the
Municipal Code and prohibit the sale or discharge of any fireworks within the City, effective July 5, 2027;
explained that the Council’s direction was to implement a phase-out approach, allowing non-profit
organizations two additional years of fundraising opportunities while they explore alternative fundraising
methods; and further noted that the Council expressed interest in potential partnerships to help supplement or
create fundraising opportunities beyond fireworks sales.

The Council engaged in a discussion regarding the manner in which the Community Special Assistance
Program is funded and what the program would look like if the City were to fully fund it. Staff responded that

 the Community Special Assistance Program is funded through a $250 application fee paid by all non-profit
organizations interested in participating in fireworks booth sales and noted that fully funding this program
would need to be established by Resolution.

Councilmembers discussed the importance of placing the decision-making authority in the hands of the
community and expressed differing viewpoints on whether the issue should be placed on the next election ballot
for voter consideration. Suggestions were made to re-evaluate potential funding sources that could be allocated
toward the Community Special Assistance Program to offset the revenue currently generated through fireworks
sales. It was also noted that a program already exists to assist organizations and that funds have been allocated
to support their work within the community. Councilmembers emphasized the importance of hearing from all
residents, not only those who may be affected by the loss of fundraising opportunities due to the proposed ban
on fireworks sales.

Questions were raised regarding the cost of placing the measure on an election ballot. Staff responded that
placing this item on a Special Election ballot would be an estimated $148,530.00.

Moved by Councilmember Mendez, seconded by Councilmember Alvarez, to table the item and agendize it for
a future meeting.
